## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `finished_at` column holds the timestamp of the latest `started` event, so running processes show their start time as their finish time. Its catalog description also says the opposite of what the SQL does. The source table has no event that marks a process as finished (`sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `'created'`, `'started'` and `'cleared'`).

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` fills the column only when the latest event is a start. Process 20 has only event 2 (`'started'`, `'2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'`), so it gets `finished_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'` even though it is still running. Process 30, whose start was followed by `'cleared'`, gets NULL. This is the reverse of "Timestamp when the process finished" (models/schema.yml:11). Did you mean to name this column `started_at`? If a finish time is what you want, which event type should mark the finish? The `event_type` check constraint at sources/process_events.sql:4 has no finished event to key on. — Anyone reading `finished_at` will count every running process as finished at the moment it started, and will see no finish time for processes that did end.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — The description says "NULL means the process has never been started." The SQL also returns NULL when a process was started and its latest event is something else. Process 30 had `'started'` (event 3) and then `'cleared'` (event 4), so it gets `finished_at` NULL even though it was started. Please change this line to match the corrected column, or the column to match this line. — People reading the docs will wrongly conclude that cleared processes were never started.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The `row_number() ... partition by process_id order by event_id desc` CTE and the `where recency = 1` filter are unchanged. As the PR description says, the model still returns one row per process, based on the latest event.
